subject: Signal governance & runbook orchestra: dashboard baselines, trace sampling, alert routing
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@scalehealth.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Signal governance initiative — telemetry inventory attached

Hi Soojin / Laura,

Thanks again for taking time last week. Per our conversation, we want to standardize how we route signals from our production services into alerting and runbooks. Primary goals: reduce alert noise, make on-call handoffs deterministic, and ensure traces give enough context for SREs to triage without hitting production consoles.

Attached is our current telemetry inventory (high level): services, dashboards, raw metric names, and current alert thresholds. We need help mapping to three things:
- Dashboard baselines (what dashboards are golden for a page + runbook link)
- Trace sampling & enrichment strategy (where to sample, tags to preserve)
- Alert routing matrix (who gets what, on-call vs paging vs SLO-breach)

Can we do a short 30-min working session this week to sketch an initial mapping? If possible please include a template runbook so we can start drafting.

Attachment: scalehealth-telemetry-inventory.csv (csv, 28KB)

Thanks,
Samantha Ortiz
Head of Platform Reliability, ScaleHealth
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@scalehealth.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Signal governance initiative — telemetry inventory attached

Thanks Samantha — got the inventory and reviewed at a high level. Laura and Ben looped here to own the runbook/alert flow design.

Proposed short agenda for the working session (30 mins):
1) Quick tour of the inventory (you) — 5 mins
2) Prioritize 3 pipelines for first pass (dashboards + traces + alerts) — 8 mins
3) Review runbook template and escalation matrix (we’ll bring draft) — 10 mins
4) Actions & owners — 7 mins

Deliverables by the end of the session: draft runbook stub per chosen pipeline, an alert routing spreadsheet outline, and recommended trace sampling targets. I attached a one-page draft runbook template (runbook-orchestra-draft.md) that focuses on: symptom, measurable signal, immediate mitigation, and postmortem triggers.

Proposed times: Wed 11/18 10:00-10:30 PT or Thu 11/19 08:00-08:30 PT. Which works for you?

Also: can your team confirm SLOs for the three highest-priority services before the call? That will help us set thresholds rather than guess.

Attachment: runbook-orchestra-draft.md (markdown, 4KB)

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Manager, CS Ops — Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Signal governance initiative — telemetry inventory attached

Looping in Jordan and Neha — Jordan to review dashboard baselines and Neha to advise on alert routing and runbook acceptance criteria.

Quick notes before the call:
- Dashboard baselines: I recommend a small set of golden dashboards per service: 1) Request health (latency + error rate), 2) Resource contention (CPU/GPU/mem for inference), 3) Cache/KV cache hit rates. Each dashboard should have a small blurb with expected range and escalation link.
- Trace sampling: default 0.5% for standard user traffic, 5% for error traces, and 100% for 5xx spike windows (we can do dynamic ramping). Ensure span tags include request_id, model_id, region, and route_id.
- Error taxonomy: group by impact class (customer-visible, internal degradation, infra) and map to playbook severity P0/P1/P2.

I uploaded a starter mapping sheet to the shared Drive (see link). Ben — can you prepare a recommended alert mapping (page vs ticket) for the 3 services Samantha flagged?

Great session this morning — thanks everyone. Summary + immediate next actions: 

1) Selected pipelines (owners):
- inference-api (owner: Samantha) — runbook stub by Thu 11/25
- model-cache (owner: Marco) — runbook stub by Thu 11/25
- request-pipeline (owner: Samantha) — runbook stub by Thu 11/25

2) Runbook template accepted: symptom → observable signal → mitigation → rollback steps → post-incident notes. Ben will merge the template into your ScaleHealth folder (see Drive link).

3) Alert routing decisions:
- Page P0 (customer-impacting availability or data corruption) to on-call SRE (pager)
- P1 (severe degradation) to SRE channel + create ticket (no immediate page unless escalation)
- P2 (low-impact or noisier signals) to ticketing only with daily digest
Ben: deliver alert-mapping-spreadsheet.xlsx with mapping for the three services by EOD Mon 11/22.

4) Trace sampling agreed: baseline 0.5%, elevated 5% on >1% error spike windows, 100% capture for condensed window post-deploy (20m). Jordan: add sample config snippet to the Drive doc.

5) Acceptance criteria for runbook: runbook must include runbook owner, pager escalation steps, and a play-by-play mitigation with exact console commands or dashboard links. Neha: will validate runbooks and mark as "accepted" in JIRA (JIRA-OPS-4521).

Attachments: alert-mapping-spreadsheet.xlsx (stub), runbook-orchestra-draft.md, scalehealth-telemetry-inventory.csv

Next meeting: Check-in Tue 11/23 09:00 PT to review runbook drafts. Please ack this thread if the summary matches your understanding or flag discrepancies inline.

Thanks — Soojin
Manager, CS Ops — Redwood Inference
